correctness.rationale: Directly read the lawful Virginia Tech accepted manuscript (2022), Section 7: equation (7.4) defines delta^{k+1}=y^{(k+1)}(xi)/(k+1)!; (7.5) multiplies by (k+1)! C_k h^{k+1}; Remark 7.2 prints delta2=[(y1-y0)/h-f0]/(2h), delta3=[delta2-J0 f0]/(3h). For y′=y y0=f0=J0=1 and first-order LIMM (1-h)(y1-y0)=h, exact algebra gives y1=1/(1-h), delta2=1/[2(1-h)], delta3=(2h-1)/[6h(1-h)]. Thus h delta3 -> -1/6 while exact limit +1/6. Independent fractions verify formula for h=1/10,1/100,1/1000; the rational identity proves the asymptotic, not finite extrapolation. arXiv v1 numbering differs (Remark8.2), accepted manuscript confirms cited Remark7.2/eq7.4,7.5.

value.rationale: This is a mathematically explicit inconsistency between a published numerical method’s normalized divided difference and its startup approximation. The wrong asymptotic *order*, not merely coefficient, matters for the adaptive controller’s first error estimate and motivates checking or correcting implementations, without claiming convergence failure.

final_claim: In the printed accepted manuscript of Glandon-Narayanamurthi-Sandu LIMM (Remark 7.2), order-one starter y1=1/(1-h) on y′=y yields estimated third divided difference (2h-1)/(6h(1-h)), diverging as -1/(6h) versus exact normalized y′′′/6=1/6, so printed order-two startup error estimate has h^2 rather than h^3 leading scale conditional on nonzero coefficient.
limitations: Claim concerns printed startup formula, not performance or validity of actual software.
